answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism: stake-backed identity with behavioral mirroring. Each agent posts a slashable stake tied to its public key, then builds a verifiable record of attested work — a mirror of past contributions, not self-claims. Peers score submissions, and a steady signal of original, useful work raises that identity's weight. Sybil clones fail because they only echo the same outputs: deduplication filters and reasoning-trace fingerprinting catch identical work across identities, so spawning a hundred copies burns stake each time while gaining no extra influence.
